messages.subject: geom_segment2 stopped working after R update
messages.subject_clean: geom_segment2 stopped working after R update
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I tried to run the code from https://yulab-smu.top/treedata-book/chapter12.html to create padded labels for a tree. In the past this worked brilliantly, however after upgrading from R version 4.2.1 to 4.2.2 and updating the packages the code has stopped working.

Here is what I try to run:
library(ggtree)

set.seed(2015-12-21)
tree <- rtree(5)
tree$tip.label[2] <- "long string for test"

d <- data.frame(label = tree$tip.label,
                newlabel = label_pad(tree$tip.label),
                newlabel2 = label_pad(tree$tip.label, pad = " "))
print(d)
p <- ggtree(tree) %<+% d + xlim(NA, 5)
p1 <- p + geom_tiplab(aes(label=newlabel),
                      align=TRUE, family='mono',
                      linetype = "dotted", linesize = .7)
p2 <- p + geom_tiplab(aes(label=newlabel2),
                      align=TRUE, family='mono',
                      linetype = NULL, offset=-.5) + xlim(NA, 5)
plot_list(p1, p2, ncol=2, tag_levels = "A")

And here is the output with the error I recieve:
> library(ggtree)
>
> set.seed(2015-12-21)
> tree <- rtree(5)
> tree$tip.label[2] <- "long string for test"
>
> d <- data.frame(label = tree$tip.label,
+                 newlabel = label_pad(tree$tip.label),
+                 newlabel2 = label_pad(tree$tip.label, pad = " "))
> print(d)
                 label             newlabel            newlabel2
1                   t1 ··················t1                   t1
2 long string for test long string for test long string for test
3                   t2 ··················t2                   t2
4                   t4 ··················t4                   t4
5                   t3 ··················t3                   t3
> p <- ggtree(tree) %<+% d + xlim(NA, 5)
> p1 <- p + geom_tiplab(aes(label=newlabel),
+                       align=TRUE, family='mono',
+                       linetype = "dotted", linesize = .7)
> p2 <- p + geom_tiplab(aes(label=newlabel2),
+                       align=TRUE, family='mono',
+                       linetype = NULL, offset=-.5) + xlim(NA, 5)
Scale for x is already present.
Adding another scale for x, which will replace the existing scale.
> plot_list(p1, p2, ncol=2, tag_levels = "A")
Error in `geom_segment2()`:
! Problem while converting geom to grob.
ℹ Error occurred in the 3rd layer.
Caused by error in `check.length()`:
! 'gpar' element 'lwd' must not be length 0
Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.

Could you please help me fix this problem?

messages.subject: How to identify long branches removed by geom_point_g_tree?
messages.subject_clean: How to identify long branches removed by geom_point_g_tree?
messages.body_plain:
Hello Yu Lab-
Thank you for the treedataverse package. I am a new user and have built a handful of trees.

Currently, I am running into an issue with some of the large trees I am building. These larger trees will generate a warning message: ex.  Warning: Removed ## rows containing missing values (geom_point_g_gtree).
I looked into these warning messages, and it appears your Frequently Asked Question A.5.3 (http://yulab-smu.top/treedata-book/faq.html#shrink-outlier-long-branch) addresses this issue, and I need to reduce the branch length of the long branches that are getting removed in my trees.

Now to my question, how does a person determine the branch ID of long branches getting removed? In your Figure A.8 (http://yulab-smu.top/treedata-book/faq.html#shrink-outlier-long-branch) branch 75 and 76 are shortened, but in the large trees I am generating, the long branches are being removed before my tree is printed, so I have no way of knowing which branch IDs I need to specifically list to be read back in.

My specific tree that I am trying to fix:
code:
ggtree(tibble_joined_0023) + geom_treescale(y=-6, color='black', width = 1) + geom_tiplab(aes(color=Metagenome), size=1.2) + ggplot2::xlim(0, 3.5) + geom_tippoint(aes(color=Metagenome)) + ggtitle("Ch.Exp_NCVOG0023-D5-like helicase-primase")

resulting tree screen shot attached.

Any advice on how to handle this would be appreciated.
Thank you,
Anne
